terminologyReview: Guideline corrections: all are accurate and stated as native instructions rather than copied English modals. (1) eo.md and be.md now say what common.md and ga.md say: in Workers, Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat fall back to English for these languages, Intl.PluralRules supports them, and Bickr uses explicit catalog patterns and rejects missing entries. This matches intl-workerd.json and InstructionTemplates, which throws on a missing message or count variant. The old "runtime formatters silently return English" wording is gone. (2) fr.md, pt.md and it.md now say that count parameters render ASCII digits, that a category does not insert million/milliard, milhão/milhões or milione/milioni, that de/di follows only the written numeral construction, and that many may match other for an all-digit numeral. This matches String(value) in instruction-template.ts and the platform labels "il y a 1 000 000 minutes", "há 1.000.000 minutos" and "1.000.000 minuti fa". (3) de.md separates positive obligations (Sie müssen) from prohibitions (dürfen nicht), states that "Darf nicht leer sein" is the form for a required nonempty value, and warns that "muss nicht" means need not. That is the correct German modal system: English "must not" maps to "darf nicht", not to "muss nicht".

Irish reference ga.md (current) is accurate and native. It names Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat as the Workers fallback, Intl.PluralRules support, and Bickr explicit patterns with missing-entry rejection. It says not to map English modals mechanically and to use "is gá dom" for stated needed actions, while noting that caithfidh and ní mór can also express practical need, which matches focloir.ie need. It requires mutation review after digits, with a neutral count label when uncertain. The current eo.md, be.md and common.md also name the Intl formatters exactly. The removed Esperanto "silently return English" wording is absent and is not a current defect.

Relative time: all ten time.* units match the resolved Unicode CLDR ga dateFields (sha256 37a5621c…) category by category, with zero mismatches. That includes the digit-based other forms ("{{count}} bliain", "{{count}} mí", "{{count}} uair an chloig"), which also cover 0 and 11–19. With a digit string a teen "déag" construction cannot be formed. Replacing the shared other pattern with a teen-only form would be wrong for 0 and 20+, so I agree not to do it. "uair an chloig" distinguishes a counted hour from an occurrence, as ga.md requires.

Other terminology: "M'fhócas" follows the standard possessive rule. mo elides to m' before a vowel or before fh + vowel (lenited fócas → fhócas with silent fh), the same pattern as the catalog's "m'fhógraí"; fócas is masculine 1st declension per teanglann. "aitheantóir" for handle and "logáil amach" for log off are accurate choices. "uirlis" for tool and "rialtán" for a Bickr control are consistent. The maximum-count units ("Ní mór do líon … a bheith {{max}} ar a mhéad") express the same ceiling as "can include at most", the same conclusion as for Russian and Arabic. "réad JSON bailí" is uniform.
uncertainties: Irish remains best effort, and my confidence in idiom and register is moderate. Open question for a native reviewer: is "de réir na ndaoine ar mian leat a shroicheadh" acceptable, or should it be the direct relative "is mian leat a shroicheadh" (optional change proposed)?

Open question: does the CLDR future one-year form "i gceann 1 bliana" (genitive, unlike past "1 bhliain ó shin") read naturally to native readers? The catalog follows CLDR exactly, and I do not propose a change.

The neutral count labels ("Is é {{count}} líon …") preserve meaning without numeral mutation. A native reviewer could later replace them with mutated noun forms per category, but only with confirmed forms for digits.

grok.terminologyReview: The current references give simple native instructions and do not copy English modal labels onto native grammar. The current eo.md and be.md name Intl.ListFormat and Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, as common.md and ga.md do. In the Workers runtime those two APIs fall back to English for Esperanto, Belarusian, and Irish. Intl.PluralRules supports their categories. Bickr catalog formatters reject a missing entry and use explicit native patterns. The current eo.md does not contain a removed runtime-formatters sentence. French, Portuguese, and Italian count parameters render as ASCII digits. A many category does not insert million, milliard, milhão, milhões, milione, or milioni. de or di is used only when the written numeral construction requires it. A many variant can match other when the numeral is entirely digits. Native Intl.RelativeTimeFormat gives a round million a direct numeric plural label in those three languages. German uses müssen for a positive obligation, nicht with the imperative for a negative command, and dürfen nicht for a prohibition. Darf nicht leer sein requires a nonempty value. muss nicht means need not. Current ga.md uses the singular imperative, An Caighdeán Oifigiúil, caithfidh tú or ní mór duit for obligation, ná for a prohibition, and is gá dom for a first-person needed action when it fits. The official need entry gives is gá, ní gá, caithfidh, and ní mór as need constructions in context. Using Is gá dom here preserves practical necessity and leaves caithfidh and ní mór available. Ní gá stays where English says do not need or need not, including the quirk sentence and the long-reply sentence in system.main. Ní féidir stays where English says cannot. The catalog year, month, day, hour, and minute patterns match the resolved CLDR dateFields file, sha256 37a5621ccb903dc8026f8a06efdd9ae244e21070bf0e88998a6026b33d02160a, with {0} written as {{count}}. The other forms are digit forms: i gceann {{count}} bliain and {{count}} bliain ó shin, i gceann {{count}} mí and {{count}} mí ó shin, i gceann {{count}} lá and {{count}} lá ó shin, i gceann {{count}} uair an chloig and {{count}} uair an chloig ó shin, and i gceann {{count}} nóiméad and {{count}} nóiméad ó shin. many hours use n-uair an chloig. No catalog pattern uses déag. Irish other includes 0 and 11–19, so a teen-only déag construction cannot replace the shared other pattern. irish-number-evidence.json says not to infer a noun form from the category name. An Caighdeán Oifigiúil sections 9.3.1, 9.3.2, and 9.3.10 distinguish numeral constructions, and section 10.2.4 says the simplified system above twenty does not lenite the noun. The maximum-count ceiling stays in the catalog outside this unit list: textTooLong uses níos mó ná {{count}} with neutral líon in all five categories, note capacity uses líon uasta, list_profiles uses uasteorainn, and system.main keeps Mermaid ar a mhéad and fad uasta mar theorainn, ní sprioc. Table 8B writes m'athair before a vowel. Section 10.2.3(a) lenites after mo. Section 10.2.5 shortens do and de to d' before a vowel or f plus a vowel, as in d'fhoghlaimeoirí, because fh is silent, and it does not shorten f plus a consonant. fócas and fógraí begin with f plus a vowel, so M'fhócas and m'fhógraí are the contracted lenited possessives. Logáil amach and d'aitheantóir remain accurate choices for log off and the handle. rialtán names a Bickr control and uirlis names a tool. Irish idiom and register remain best effort. Agreement of í and di with the feminine noun pearsa is noun gender. These supplied sentences leave no open wording question.

uncertainties: Irish idiom and register remain best effort without a human native review. The time patterns follow resolved Unicode CLDR digit forms, including the other category for zero and 11–19. Neutral count labels favor explicit meaning over uncertain numeral inflection.

previousDecision.leadReason: Use suim for concern or interest in another participant’s activity, with the explicit permission not to like the person. Cúram can express care, but its responsibility or anxiety senses can make the follow criterion less clear. This is a native wording choice rather than a claim that cúram cannot mean care. Preserve the only-if follow criterion and every other source condition, role, example, and limit.
previousDecision.candidateReason: Opus preserves conditions and exceptions with better Irish clauses. Restore autonomous participant rather than independent participation, recent threads rather than new, and backticks rather than back heads. Grok mistranslates max length and leaves villain; Gemini weakens cycles to advice and changes unsociable to idle.
previousDecision.opusReason: Every line was checked against the English: simulation notice and both never rules, roles, decisions, the no-reason repeat ban, activities, audience and blogs, follow rules, refs and replies, duplicate-reply rules, Markdown, Mermaid, SVG and math limits, the ‼️ override and length guidance all match. One wording risk: line 47 renders "care about their activity" as "más cúram leat a ghníomhaíocht" and "cúram a bheith ort faoi". Cúram leans toward responsibility or charge rather than interest, so the follow criterion can read as "if their activity is your responsibility". Codex, grok and gemini use suim (interest), which carries the English meaning clearly. This is marked optional because my Irish confidence on the idiom is limited.
previousDecision.grokReason: Accept. Mermaid ní mór ... ar a mhéad keeps must-at-most. Hot stays móréilimh. Cycles stay ní cheadaítear ... timthriallta. SVG and math keep their within-limit instructions. The math fence and the two-backslash sentence stay exact. {{nativeLanguage}} joins the display-name sentence and {{persona}}{{setting}} stays glued. opus.reason: I re-checked the whole prompt against the frozen source. The 139 unchanged lines are identical to the text both reviewers accepted, including the suim/dúil follow criterion already adopted. The four changed lines are faithful. (1) "Deir fógraí séanta feiceálacha é sin" is correct: focloir.ie gives "disclaimer notice = fógra séanta", and teanglann lists séanadh with genitive séanta and no plural. So the old bare plural "séanta" was unsupported, and "fógraí séanta" (plural notices with a genitive modifier, plural adjective feiceálacha) is the right plural. (2) "sroich" for reaching people is attested in focloir.ie reach sense 5 ("affect, influence: sroich, téigh chomh fada le") and avoids "teacht ar" (come upon or find). "chun níos mó daoine a shroicheadh" is correct, and the actor is explicit in "leat". (3) "Ná téigh i gcoinne na pearsantachta, na staire, na gcreideamh ná na tuairisce a bhaineann le do phearsa. Ná seachain iad." has correct genitives after i gcoinne (pearsantachta, staire, gen. pl. eclipsed gcreideamh, tuairisce) and keeps both prohibitions (contradict, evade) and "you cannot change that description". One optional grammar point remains, which is not a meaning defect. In "de réir na ndaoine ar mian leat a shroicheadh" the antecedent "daoine" is the direct object of the verbal noun, so standard Irish uses the direct relative "is mian leat a shroicheadh". This catalog already does so in "an cuardach is mian liom a dhéanamh" (tools.log_off) and "is mian leat a dhéanamh" (system.logOffInstruction). "ar mian" would normally need a resumptive pronoun ("ar mian leat iad a shroicheadh"). My Irish confidence here is moderate; the lead decides.

grok.reason: Accept the four changed lines. I compared the full proposed text with every frozen English clause. Line 4 uses fógraí séanta feiceálacha for prominent disclaimers. teanglann.ie lists séanadh as a masculine noun, nominative séanadh and genitive séanta, so séanta is the genitive modifier and feiceálacha agrees with plural fógraí.
